description: The Icelandic Electronic Communications Office publishes a set of spatial layers through the Natural Science and Land Survey map viewer and the Icelandic geoportal. Coverage layers show modelled service areas for GSM, TETRA, 3G, 4G and 5G of Síminn, Nova, Vodafone and the emergency line Neyðarlínan (TETRA), modelled for outdoor signal at 2 metres height, with a separate high speed mobile layer from January 2022. Road measurement layers hold drive tests of GSM, 3G, 4G and TETRA along the main road network, made mostly from autumn 2015 to autumn 2017 for the telecommunications fund. Infrastructure layers give counts of mobile, microwave, DVB-T and FM, and TETRA transmitters per grid cell, a description of the office's register of communications installations with their locations, the route and owners of fibre optic cables within 1 km squares, and older fibre and copper layers. Further layers show a 50 nautical mile band at sea and popular tourist places used in coverage assessments. Coverage: Iceland and its coastal waters. Format and access: map viewer, geoportal metadata and some downloads through shared drive folders, free; no licence was stated. Caveats: several layers date from 2016 to 2022; transmitter data are aggregated to grid cells; downloads sit on third-party drives. Simulation uses: coverage along roads and at sea, emergency radio reach and fibre route exposure for Icelandic hazard models such as volcanic eruptions and storms. Related records: the Nordic and Baltic telecom market statistics give Icelandic totals; Finnsenderen gives Norwegian transmitter sites.
